What’s new

Release notes.

A running record of what’s changed in Doceo.

0.7.0October 22, 2026Latest

Four kinds of document

  • Notes and Pages are now separate documents — no more Note | Page switch. Convert one into the other when you want to
  • Slides (.pptx) and Sheets (.xlsx) join them, each with a full editor, a format panel, a command search and pop-out windows
  • Open .pptx and .xlsx files in place from the Files page; any other file opens in the app your system uses for it, with Open with… on right-click

Over a hundred templates

  • One gallery (Ctrl+Shift+N) for notes, pages, slides and sheets, plus new whiteboard and database templates

Work the way you like

  • Split view: two or three documents side by side, with grouped, numbered tabs and a resizable divider
  • The + in the tab strip asks which kind of document to make
  • Spelling, grammar and AutoCorrect in Notes, Pages and Slides; the Pages engine is updated to the latest version
  • Goals can read a key result from a sheet cell; Calendar and Tasks can create any kind of document; search understands is:sheet and kind:slides

Easier to read and use

  • Settings → Accessibility: text size, contrast, simple view, readable font, line spacing, bigger buttons, a strong focus outline and reduced motion
  • Twenty themes with five colours each, smoother motion, a trash bin with right-click restore and empty
  • Help & Support now opens the new, illustrated documentation on this website
0.6.4October 2026

Databases

  • Turn pages into tables, boards, galleries, lists, calendars and timelines. Save as many views as you like on one database, each with its own filters, sorting, grouping and visible columns
  • Relations and rollups link databases together; formula columns calculate from the other columns of a row (a small, safe formula language with text, number, list and date functions)
  • Bulk edit rows, export a view as CSV, and put a live view of any database inside a page with /database. Each page shows the database fields it belongs to, editable in place
  • Databases is opt-in: Settings → Features

Bring your work in

  • Import a folder or .zip from Obsidian or plain Markdown, Notion or Confluence: folders, pages, links between pages and images come across, and your originals are never touched
  • Notion databases (CSV) become real Doceo databases, with typed columns, rows matched to their pages, and table, board and calendar views
  • Import a Jira CSV export into Tasks — projects, ticket keys, issue types, epics, sub-tasks, comments, labels and sprints; importing again skips what you already have

Tasks, Jira-style

  • Projects get a ticket key and tasks are numbered like APP-12; tasks can be a Task, Bug, Story or Epic, and epics show progress for the tasks in them
  • Link tasks (blocks, relates to, duplicates) — a task with an unfinished blocker is flagged “Blocked”
  • Sprints with a goal, dates, progress and a burndown; completing one moves unfinished work to the backlog or the next sprint
  • Saved filters in the left bar

Daily notes and quick capture

  • Ctrl+J opens today’s daily note, with unfinished items carried over from the last one; right-click a day in the Calendar to open any other day’s note
  • Ctrl+Shift+Space captures a thought anywhere in the app into today’s note, as a task, or as a new page

Everywhere else

  • Note view and Page view now share the default font and size, and changes in one show in the other
  • Renaming is reliable again: double-click a name or use the right-click menu or the breadcrumb, and Backspace at the end of a name edits it instead of opening it
  • Databases, Whiteboards, project and template tiles follow the same folder-and-page tile look
  • Archive and restore a page from the ••• menu
  • A completely rewritten Help & Support page: a searchable guide to every part of the app, every shortcut, and answers to common questions
0.6.3October 2026

Folders and pages that look like folders and pages

  • A folder is now a folder: a large tile in its own colour with the name and note count inside in text that always reads, and the pages sticking out when it has notes in it (none for an empty folder, up to three for a full one)
  • Notes show as portrait pages with the title, a few lines of the note and the date; a coloured note gets a tint and a coloured top edge. Dashboard “Recent notes” keep their compact rows
  • Both appear on All notes and folder pages, Unsorted, Recent, label pages, Trash and the dashboard’s Folders card, and are a little smaller than before

On the Mac

  • Double-click empty space on the top bar to zoom the window to fit the screen, and again to go back — the way other Mac apps do (it is not full screen)
0.6.2October 2026

macOS first. Windows and Linux builds follow.

  • This release is out for macOS now; the Windows and Linux installers are still on 0.6.0 and will follow

A calmer look

  • The window is now one flush layout: the top bar, sidebar and page meet in straight lines with no gaps, like a native app; cards, menus and dialogs keep their rounded boxes
  • One type and spacing system everywhere: consistent sizes, readable sentence-case group labels, and the same margins and card spacing on every page
  • A back button that really goes back — to the page, folder, label, whiteboard or note you came from (Ctrl+[ too)
  • Doceo opens with a softly breathing skeleton that gives way to your workspace, piece by piece

Whiteboards

  • A full diagram editor: about 60 shapes, connectors that stay attached (straight, elbow or curved, with draggable waypoints), tables, sticky notes, containers and swimlanes, layers, multiple pages, auto layout and a hand-drawn look
  • Every template now shows a preview, with its name and description; the editor sits under your tabs and shows its real path (Doceo › Whiteboards › board name)
  • Formatted labels, links on shapes, page cards and live task cards; import draw.io files, Mermaid flowcharts and outlines; export PNG, SVG, draw.io or JSON; version history
  • Put a diagram inside any page with /diagram, like draw.io in Confluence; whiteboard text is searchable

Pages and wiki features

  • Sub-pages (a page tree), smart embeds for video, Figma and Google files, an Insights page, bulk actions and merging, find and replace across every page, and optional Databases (Settings › Features)
  • Export a folder as a small website with a menu and search

Safer and more reliable

  • Saving is safer: overlapping saves can no longer damage a note, a failed save shows a clear warning, and a damaged file is set aside and reported instead of silently disappearing
  • Imported diagrams and files are checked before they are drawn, links are limited to safe kinds, embeds run sandboxed, and the app enforces a strict content policy
  • Calendar subscriptions refresh while you work anywhere in the app, not only on the Calendar page; the event dialog styling is fixed
  • Accessibility: every top-bar button has a name and click targets are bigger
0.6.0October 2026

Doceo for iPhone

  • A phone app built for the phone: Dashboard, Notes, Calendar and Tasks in one tab bar, with the same look as the desktop app
  • Notes like Apple Notes — folders, a dated list with pinned notes, swipe and press-and-hold actions, a keyboard bar for formatting, checklists, tables and photos
  • A simple calendar: a month with the day’s agenda, or one day as a timeline; add events with quick words like “Lunch fri 1pm”; Outlook, Teams and link calendars with join buttons
  • Tasks as live widgets, a status list and a day-by-day timeline; swipe back and forward between screens from the screen edges; portrait only
  • The iPhone app is not on the App Store yet — it is built from source with Xcode

Dashboard

  • The Exports card lists the files you saved with Export, and a new Calendars card shows every connected calendar and when it last synced

Faster and sturdier

  • Starts with about two-thirds less code to load; editors and pages load the moment you need them
  • Repeating events that began years ago always show up; very long titles no longer stretch the Dashboard; calendar links are checked before they are added
  • Safer links from calendar invites, and large page renders are capped to protect memory
0.5.1October 2026

Export where you want

  • Exports now work like Save As in Word: pick the folder and name in the Save dialog for PDF, Word, Markdown and more — Doceo no longer saves into a folder of its own
  • Files → Exports remembers where each export went; open it from there to view or edit it in place, show it in its folder, or remove it from the list

Smoother on Windows & Linux

  • Page view sends compressed page pictures, and only for pages that changed — the app no longer stalls on small actions like adding a table or changing a colour
  • Saving and loading notes no longer blocks the window; lighter panels on Windows and Linux; a renderer fix for Linux
  • PDFs from Note view now go through the Save dialog on Windows and Linux too, and pulled-out windows have a properly padded title
0.5.0October 2026

Open real files, in tabs

  • Open .docx, .odt, .rtf, Markdown, text and HTML files from anywhere on your disk, edit them in place and save back to the same file; PDFs open in a viewer. Older .doc files save as .docx beside the original
  • A new Files page: open files or whole folders, recent files, and your exports in one place
  • Documents open in tabs with breadcrumbs (under the tabs or in the top bar — your choice in Settings), and closing a tab with unsaved changes asks first
  • Drag tabs to reorder them, or pull one out into its own window with the full toolbar — and drop it back onto the tab bar to dock it again

Windows & Linux

  • Minimise, maximise and close buttons at the right of the app bar, in the main window and in pulled-out document windows

Tasks & Calendar

  • The Timeline is now a proper Gantt chart: task names stay pinned on the left while the chart scrolls, today is highlighted in a rounded box, and paging weeks back or forward keeps every task on its date
  • Cleaner lines under the Calendar and Tasks toolbars, and a text-colour menu with a dropdown in the editor

Simplified

  • The Copilot side panel, Favourites and the Highlights page are gone, to keep Doceo focused on your documents (the text highlight tool stays)
0.4.0October 2026

A new identity

  • A new app logo — three stacked cards in mint, white and black with a soft glossy finish — in the Dock, taskbar, installers and the website
  • New favicon for the website and the in-app web view
0.3.0October 2026

A fresh look

  • A flat, light-by-default design: floating panels, tighter corners, Geist type and a green accent — all 20 themes kept
  • Invisible scrollbars everywhere, with scrolling unchanged
  • A better top bar: one sidebar toggle in the same place open or closed, windowed or full screen

Dashboard, Settings and Help

  • A new Dashboard above All notes: recent notes, folders, tasks, calls, calendar, favourites, highlights and exports
  • Real Settings and Help & Support pages, plus working Search (Ctrl+K) and shortcuts

Calendar & platforms

  • Sign in with Microsoft 365 to bring your Teams meetings into the calendar (read-only)
  • A redesigned Add calendar dialog
  • Linux installers: AppImage, .deb and .rpm, alongside Windows and macOS
0.2.0October 2026

A new editor

  • Page view rebuilt on a new document engine, with real .docx files saved alongside your notes
  • One floating toolbar and one Format panel, identical in Note and Page view, with a smooth animated switch
  • Pictures and shapes: select, move and resize; header and footer by double-clicking a margin
  • Pinch-to-zoom, a rich right-click menu, and a responsive toolbar that adapts to the window
  • Neutral shortcuts — Ctrl-based on every platform

Tasks & Calendar

  • A project board with Overview, Board, List, Table and Timeline views
  • Tasks linked to documents, with subtasks, comments and activity
  • A Teams-style calendar with .ics subscriptions for Outlook, Google and iCloud

Library

  • Favourites for notes and folders; restorable Trash on the tile grid
  • An Exports folder that collects PDF and Word exports
  • Copilot is now a rounded side panel; a tidier top bar and sidebar
0.1.0July 2026

First release

  • Local-first notes and folders with drag-and-drop organisation
  • Rich text editor with tables, images, headers and footers, and find & replace
  • Native in-app PDF export on macOS and Word export
  • 20+ themes and macOS & Windows installers

Write it. Plan it. Keep it.
